newsitem.title: USA: Iowa corn, soybean crops receive welcome rain.
newsitem.headline: Iowa corn, soybean crops receive welcome rain.

text.p: Iowa's corn and soybean crops received welcome weekend rains as dry weather and cool nighttime temperatures were beginning to slow crop progress, according to the Iowa Agricultural Statistics Service.
But many corn fields were in need of more rain as that crop enters the critical pollination stage of development, according to the report.
Corn had tasseled on two percent of the state's acreage, the same pace as 1996 but eight days behind the five-year average of 13 percent.
Corn conditions declined from a week ago and were one percent very poor, two percent poor, 18 percent fair, 58 percent good and 21 percent excellent as of Friay.
Soybeans were blooming in Iowa with 33 percent of the acreage in bloom as of Sunday. That is five days ahead of 1996 and one day ahead of the five-year average.
The soybean condition also declined last week to one percent very poor, four percent poor, 24 percent fair, 57 percent good and 14 percent excellent as of Friday.

Topsoil moisture as of Friday was four percent very short, 24 percent short, 69 percent adequate and three percent surplus. Subsoil moisture was one percent very short, 16 percent short, 79 percent adequate and four percent surplus.
